findings.description: The user_data script exports a static AWS access key ID and secret access key in cleartext. EC2 user data is retrievable through the instance metadata service (including via SSRF from the public-facing web app) and is stored unencrypted in the instance configuration and in Terraform state, allowing credential theft and lateral movement.

The instance is launched in a public subnet with map_public_ip_on_launch = true and an internet-gateway route, attached to a security group open to 0.0.0.0/0 on SSH and HTTP, giving the internet direct reachability to a host that carries long-lived AWS credentials.

No metadata_options block is set, so IMDSv1 (token-optional) remains enabled. Combined with credentials in user data and a publicly reachable web service, this makes credential exfiltration via SSRF straightforward.
No root_block_device with encrypted = true is specified, so the root EBS volume — which holds the user-data-derived secrets and application data — may be created unencrypted.

Ingress on TCP/22 is permitted from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing SSH administrative access to the entire internet on a host that holds hard-coded AWS credentials, enabling brute-force and exploitation attempts.
Port 80 is open to 0.0.0.0/0 and the user_data provisions only a plain Apache HTTP listener with no TLS, so application traffic is served unencrypted over the internet.
Egress allows all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0, providing an unrestricted channel for data exfiltration and command-and-control if the internet-facing host is compromised.
The EBS volume attached to the web host does not set encrypted = true (the attribute is deliberately commented out), so block storage data is written unencrypted.
The snapshot is taken from an unencrypted volume and inherits that state, so a copy of the volume data persists unencrypted and can be shared or restored across accounts without KMS key controls.
The VPC flow log destination bucket defines no server_side_encryption_configuration, so network telemetry containing internal addressing and traffic metadata is stored without enforced encryption.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block, ACL restriction, or bucket policy is defined, so prevention of public exposure of flow log data relies entirely on account-level defaults.

The bucket has no policy requiring aws:SecureTransport, so log objects may be read or written over cleartext HTTP; combined with force_destroy = true and no versioning, audit data integrity is weakly protected.

map_public_ip_on_launch = true causes every instance in this subnet to receive a public IP, and the associated route table routes 0.0.0.0/0 to an internet gateway, removing the network boundary between workloads and the internet.
map_public_ip_on_launch = true causes every instance in this subnet to receive a public IP, and it shares the internet-gateway route table, eliminating private-subnet segmentation.

The VPC's default security group is not locked down with an aws_default_security_group resource, so any resource inadvertently launched without an explicit group inherits the default allow-all-from-self and all-egress rules rather than an explicit deny.
